transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My clinic doctor kind of pushed me to come in. She’s been on me about how I’m eating. I guess most days I keep it pretty simple—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and then a small dinner if I’m not too busy with class paperwork.
Do you find yourself wanting to eat more, but something stops you, or do you just not feel like eating most of the time?

I don’t know that I really want more and then stop myself. Most days I just keep it basic—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites while I’m between jobs, and then a small dinner later if I’m not caught up with class paperwork. It just feels like that’s enough, I guess.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Yeah, I guess some. My work pants are definitely looser than they used to be, and people at job sites have said I look too thin. I don’t really see it that way, though—I figured I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Are you worried about gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like saying it that way, but yes. If I eat something really heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling that I’m going to wake up bigger or slower. Like I won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms the way I need to for work.
Do you think about your weight or body shape when you decide what to eat or how much to eat?

Yeah, I do. I think about whether something is going to make me feel bigger or heavier. If it’s something like pizza or a big sandwich, I get anxious that I’ll wake up feeling bigger and slower, and then I won’t be able to move around ladders or work the way I need to.
Do you ever eat until you feel uncomfortably full?
Not really. I mean, I usually stop before I get to that point. I don’t like feeling overly full, so I try to avoid that.
Do you worry that if you start eating a lot, you won't be able to stop?
I don’t think that’s really the issue for me. I’m usually trying not to eat too much, so I haven’t really had that feeling of being unable to stop.
Do you feel like you would lose control if you allowed yourself to eat as much as you want?
I’m not sure. I don’t really let myself eat that much, so I don’t know what would happen. I don’t think about it like I’d completely lose control, it’s more that I try not to get to that point.
Do you think you would be happier if you weighed a bit more?

No, not really. The idea of weighing more makes me nervous. Like if I eat something heavy, pizza or a big sandwich, I start thinking I’m going to wake up bigger or slower, and then I won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms at work the way I need to.
Do you feel anxious about eating because you're worried you might not be able to control how much you eat once you start?

I don’t think that’s the main anxiety for me. It’s not like I start eating and worry I won’t stop. I’m more just careful before I eat, and I try to keep it from getting to a point where I feel uncomfortable.
Do you think your eating habits are controlled by a fear of losing control over the amount you eat?
I don’t think so, not exactly. I don’t really feel like I’m afraid I’ll lose control once I start eating. It’s more that I try to keep things measured and not let myself get uncomfortable.
Do you think your eating habits are aimed at maintaining a certain weight or body shape?

Yeah, I think so. I try to keep myself from getting heavier. If I eat something like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this panicky feeling that I’ll wake up bigger and slower, and then I won’t be able to move around ladders or tight rooms at work the way I need to.
Have you had a significant amount of weight loss over the past few months?

Yeah, I mean… my work pants are definitely looser than they used to be. They kind of hang on me now. People on job sites have said I look too thin, but I guess I’ve been seeing it more like I’ve just leaned out from being on my feet all day.
Does your fear of gaining weight affect your daily activities or relationships outside of work?

Yeah, somewhat. I’m still going to jobs and my classes, so it’s not like I’ve stopped everything. But I have started avoiding lunches with coworkers, or study meetups, because it’s just easier to stick to my routine and not have people watching or commenting on what I’m eating.
Do you think you look too thin, or do you still see yourself as being at a normal weight?

I don’t really see it as some emergency the way other people seem to. I know people say I look too thin, but to me it feels more like I’m just being disciplined and busy, not like there’s something seriously wrong with my weight.
Do you make a conscious effort to restrict your calorie intake?

Yeah… I guess I do, in a way. I’m here because the clinic doctor was getting on me about how little I’m eating. Most days I just keep it pretty simple—coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between jobs, and then a small dinner if I’m not too tied up with class paperwork.
Is your main goal in limiting what you eat to avoid gaining weight or to achieve a certain body shape?

I think it’s mostly to avoid gaining weight. Like, if I eat something heavy—pizza or a big sandwich—I get this panicky feeling that I’m going to wake up bigger and slower. And then I worry I won’t be able to move around ladders and rooms the way I need to for work.
Is your goal of avoiding heavy meals, like pizza or big sandwiches, primarily because you fear gaining weight or because you want to maintain a specific body shape for your work?

It’s more the fear of gaining weight, honestly. I’m not really thinking about some specific shape for work. It’s like if I eat something heavy, I panic that I’ll wake up bigger and heavier, and then I won’t be able to move around on ladders or in rooms the way I need to.
Do you think you look too thin, even when other people tell you that you do?

I mean, not really. I know people say I look too thin, but I don’t see it as some emergency the way they do. To me it feels like they’re making a big deal out of it, like I’m just disciplined and busy.
Is your goal of eating less about achieving a certain body shape or just about not gaining weight?

It’s more about not gaining weight. I’m not trying to get some certain shape. It’s just that if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get really panicky that I’ll wake up bigger and slower, and then I won’t be able to move around at work like I need to.
